# Free Computation Foundation

Website: https://freecomputation.org/

> The Free Computation Foundation promotes and defends the freedom to compute. The free software movement freed the code; free computation asks the next question — the program is free, but is the computing? When computation is rented from clouds, sealed into devices, and metered through APIs, freedom is lost without any license changing. The Foundation's test: pull the network cable — if it stops working, it was never yours.

## Stance

- The Foundation is not a political movement: no culture-war positions, no feuds, no provocations for an audience. It is judged by its work — software that exists, results that check out, knowledge anyone can use. Its programs are standing work being built and published, not protest campaigns.

## The Four Freedoms of Computation

- Freedom 0 — Compute without permission: run any computation, for any purpose; no account, activation, or authority.
- Freedom 1 — Compute on your own machine: locally, offline, on hardware that answers to you from the firmware up.
- Freedom 2 — Verify what was computed: reproduce results exactly; exact results, approximations, and conjectures are always labelled as which they are. Certainty is never manufactured.
- Freedom 3 — Share the computation: publish programs, data, and results for anyone to run and check; a computation's output belongs to the one who computed it, without obligation.

## Programs

- Own Your Machine: libre boot firmware and hardware that takes its owner's instructions.
- Offline Is a Right: offline-first tools with full capability and no network, account, or vendor.
- Exact or Labelled: exact arithmetic, reproducible builds, differential proof as everyday practice.
- Output Is Yours: formats and licenses that attach no obligations to a computation's output.
- Open Proof: public research observatories; a census is not a verification record.
- Compute for Everyone: good maths should be free — tools and teaching with no money, permission, or connection required.

## Projects

- [GitHub](https://github.com/freecomputation): all Foundation projects, built in the open
- CENTL / CentL26: exact-first offline scientific workbench (mathematics, physics, chemistry) — exact rational arithmetic, symbolic calculus, notebooks, offline natural-language solver. Begun under NIGHTWARE LABZ; continues here.
- Krell: a machine-facing portable assembly — typed SSA with block arguments, total semantics, hash-consed binary encoding, verifiable, faster than C on its certified record (krell.cc). Its Encoding Exception keeps encoded programs free of license obligations.
- Erdős–Straus Observatory: open research on 4/p = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z; status OPEN.

## Support

- There is no membership tier, tip jar, or sponsor scheme. The Foundation is sustained by work: running the tools, checking the proofs, contributing computation, code, and counterexamples.
